title: Claude Code vs Cursor: When to Use Each (and When to Use Both)
summary: Claude Code is a terminal AI agent. Cursor is an AI-powered IDE. Here's the honest breakdown of both — plus a third option most developers end up wanting.
body_markdown: Claude Code is purpose-built for this. Its whole-project context model via CLAUDE.md means it reasons across the full repo without manual file feeding. Cursor handles large codebases well for navigation and targeted edits, but Agent mode context is bounded by what you` @` -mention explicitly. For large codebases where you want to ship a new feature end-to-end, Claude Code's autonomous model wins.[Blink](https://blink.new/) lets you import a repo and extend it with database, auth, and API layers — so large existing codebases can gain full-stack infrastructure without starting from scratch.
